Cc: Chris Taylor <ctaylor@orchidlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Production surge — latency and 5xx spike affecting checkout

Hi Ben,

We observed a sustained latency increase and a spike in 5xx errors from ~08:40–09:05 PT this morning that impacted checkout conversion across two regions. Our SREs captured increased tail latency (p95->p99) and a correlated drop in throughput on your /generate endpoint. Can you confirm this is being tracked as a customer incident and share next steps? Orchid is evaluating mitigation options now — we need an RCA and short remediation plan for our leadership (tomorrow EOD).

Asha
Asha Menon
Head of Infrastructure, Orchid Labs

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Asha Menon <asha@orchidlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:03:51 -07:00
Subject: Orchid Labs — RCA draft and immediate mitigations (v0.9)

Ben / team / Asha,

Attached is the initial RCA (orchid_rca_v1.pdf) and a sample traffic capture. Summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: a small subset of long-context requests (token lengths > 6k) triggered cache fragmentation in the serving runtime leading to degraded batching efficiency and increased OOM-driven retries on one GPU pool.
- Observable effect: elevated p95/p99 latency, higher retry rates causing transient 502/503 responses; throughput for the affected model dropped ~37% during the window.
- Immediate mitigations applied: suppressed large-context batching for the affected pool, hot-restarted the node group, and deployed a temporary routing rule to shift new sessions to a healthy variant.

Action items (owner, ETA):
1) Grace O'Connor — complete action tracker with per-route fallback config and rollback runbook — ETA 2027-05-18 EOD
2) Markus Klein — add protective mem-threshold and alert to prevent OOM-driven retries — ETA 2027-05-17 COB
3) Kim (me) — finalize RCA doc and coordinate exec readout slide deck — ETA 2027-05-16 morning

Asha: please find the RCA PDF attached. We propose an exec readout on Tuesday 2027-05-18 10:00 PT to walk leadership through root cause and the closure plan.

Kimberly Park
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: orchid_rca_v1.pdf, orchid_traffic_sample-20270514.log

From: Asha Menon <asha@orchidlabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Kim / Ben — thank you for the fast turnaround and the clear mitigation steps. A few clarifying items from Orchid:
- Can you confirm whether any customer data was retried to other regions? Orchid is concerned about ordering and duplicate writes in checkout paths.
- For the proposed routing to a healthy variant, please include the expected performance delta and any cost/reliability tradeoffs.

We can do the exec readout on 2027-05-18 10:00 PT; I will loop in our CIO for that meeting. We also need a deliverable (action tracker) we can review by EOD 2027-05-17 so our engineering leadership can sign off on the longer-term changes.

Asha

Quick reply from Chris Taylor (one-line): "thanks team — appreciate the transparency, priority from our side is preventing duplicate-checkout writes."

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@orchidlabs.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 15:06:12 -07:00
Subject: Action tracker and closure cadence for Orchid Labs surge (ATTACHED)

Hi Asha — attaching the tracker (orchid_action_tracker.xlsx) with owners, priorities, and acceptance criteria. Highlights:
- Short-term (blockers): mem-threshold, per-route fallback, and an urgent audit of retry/duplicate logic — owners and ETA populated.
- Medium-term: model quantization profile adjustments and KV cache compaction work to prevent fragmentation — target sprint: June sprint 2.
- Closure criteria: 4 consecutive days of p99 < baseline+25ms and zero duplicate-write incidents after the new retry gating is live.

Can you confirm Orchid can accept the short-term acceptance criteria by EOD 2027-05-18? If so we will lock the migration window for the protective routing on 2027-05-20 03:00 PT (low-traffic).

Ben

Attachments: orchid_action_tracker.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Asha Menon <asha@orchidlabs.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec readout summary — closure scheduled and follow-through notes

Team — quick summary post-readout: execs from Orchid and Redwood joined 2027-05-18 readout; leadership validated root cause and the closure path. Agreed next steps:
- Protective routing applied 2027-05-20 03:00 PT, observed immediate restoration of throughput and p99 within expected bounds.
- Follow-through sprint (June sprint 2) includes KV compaction and mem-threshold hardening.
- Weekly checkpoints until closure (owner: Grace O'Connor) — first checkpoint 2027-05-24.

Attached: updated action tracker (we updated acceptance criteria to include post-migration warmup verification and a duplicate-write audit).

Thanks everyone for tight coordination. I will continue to own the RCA doc and will publish version 1.1 with post-mitigation metrics by 2027-05-22.

Kimberly Park
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
